newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo troops take arms from opposition faction.
newsitem.headline: New Congo troops take arms from opposition faction.

text.p: Troops in the Democratic Republic of Congo capital fired in the air on Friday and confiscated weapons from members of a breakaway opposition faction who also fired in the air, witnesses said.
Two bodyguards from the faction, led by Kibassa Maliba, were arrested after being found with arms in a search of Kibassa's house and office in the Limite suburb of Kinshasa.
Kibassa broke away from veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress party in 1996 and moved closer to ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Several hundred of Tshisekedi's supporters on Friday marched through Kinshasa to protest against newly-installed President Laurent Kabila and the presence of Rwandan troops among his forces who drove Mobutu out almost two weeks ago.

Soldiers of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo allowed the demonstrators to march as far as Tshisekedi's house, which is only a few hundred metres (yards) from Kibassa's residence.
Witnesses said Tshisekedi's supporters later moved toward Kibassa's house where they taunted his bodyguards and encouraged Alliance troops to search the building.
